questions.question: In the MacDonald and Martineau study on mood and intentions to have unprotected sex, which variable was NOT directly measured?

answers.text: Self-esteem
Mood
Intentions to have unprotected sex
Actual sexual behavior

questions.question: What is measurement defined as in psychological research?

answers.text: The assignment of scores to individuals so that the scores represent some characteristic of the individuals
The use of standardized instruments to collect data
The observation of behavior in controlled laboratory settings
The statistical analysis of numerical data

questions.question: Which of the following is a key reason why psychological constructs cannot be directly observed?

answers.text: They are too complex to study scientifically
They often represent tendencies to think, feel, or act in certain ways
They can only be measured using physiological equipment
They are purely theoretical concepts with no behavioral manifestations

questions.question: In the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale, how are items 3, 5, 8, 9, and 10 scored differently from items 1, 2, 4, 6, and 7?

answers.text: They use a different rating scale
They are weighted more heavily in the total score
Their scoring is reversed
They are optional items that may be skipped

questions.question: What is a conceptual definition?

answers.text: A definition that describes how a variable will be measured
A definition that describes the behaviors and internal processes that make up a construct and how it relates to other variables
A dictionary definition of a psychological term
A statistical formula for calculating a construct score

questions.question: In Bandura's Bobo doll study, the operational definition of physical aggression was:

answers.text: Children's self-reported feelings of anger
The number of specifically defined aggressive acts committed during a 20-minute period
Teachers' ratings of children's overall aggressiveness
Physiological measures of arousal during play

questions.question: What is the purpose of using converging operations in psychological research?

answers.text: To reduce the cost of conducting research studies
To use multiple operational definitions that 'converge' on the same construct
To ensure that all researchers use identical measurement procedures
To combine different statistical analyses into a single result

questions.question: At which level of measurement are category labels assigned without any implied ordering?

answers.text: Ordinal
Nominal
Interval
Ratio

questions.question: Which level of measurement has equal intervals but lacks a true zero point?

answers.text: Nominal
Ordinal
Interval
Ratio

questions.question: Why is IQ considered to be measured at the interval level rather than the ratio level?

answers.text: IQ scores cannot be ranked from lowest to highest
A score of 0 does not represent the complete absence of intelligence, and ratios are not meaningful
IQ tests use only categorical data
The differences between IQ scores are not equal throughout the scale

questions.question: Test-retest reliability is most appropriately assessed for constructs that are:

answers.text: Expected to change rapidly over time
Assumed to be consistent across time
Measured only once in a research study
Categorical in nature

questions.question: Internal consistency refers to:

answers.text: The consistency of scores across different time periods
The consistency of people's responses across items on a multiple-item measure
The consistency of different researchers' observations
The consistency between self-report and behavioral measures

questions.question: What statistic represents the mean of all possible split-half correlations for a set of items?

answers.text: Cohen's kappa
Pearson's r
Cronbach's alpha
The standard deviation

questions.question: Face validity is best described as:

answers.text: The extent to which a measure covers the full range of a construct
The extent to which a measure appears 'on its face' to measure the construct of interest
The extent to which scores correlate with other relevant variables
The most important type of validity evidence

questions.question: Which type of validity is demonstrated when a new measure of test anxiety is negatively correlated with exam performance?

answers.text: Face validity
Content validity
Criterion validity
Internal validity

questions.question: When Cacioppo and Petty showed that scores on the Need for Cognition Scale were positively correlated with scores on existing measures of similar constructs, they were demonstrating:

answers.text: Discriminant validity
Convergent validity
Face validity
Test-retest reliability

questions.question: Discriminant validity is demonstrated when:

answers.text: Multiple items on a scale are highly correlated with each other
Scores on a measure are NOT correlated with measures of conceptually distinct variables
A measure produces consistent scores over time
Different observers agree on their ratings of behavior

questions.question: What is socially desirable responding?

answers.text: When participants respond in ways they believe are socially appropriate rather than truthfully
When participants respond in ways that please their friends
When researchers design questions that are easy to answer
When participants respond consistently across multiple measures

questions.question: According to the chapter, why is it generally better for a measure to include multiple items rather than a single item?

answers.text: Multiple items are easier for participants to understand
Multiple items improve both content validity and reliability
Multiple items require less time to administer
Multiple items are always more valid than single items

questions.question: The Ten-Item Personality Inventory (TIPI) measures all Big Five personality dimensions with only 10 items. A researcher might choose this measure when:

answers.text: Maximum reliability and validity are the highest priorities
Testing time is severely limited
Participants have limited reading ability
The study requires physiological measures
